title: Respect upower's "should be ignored" tag when determining whether or not to notify about low battery
line: Mice and keyboards that only report a rough battery level no longer show “Battery Low” popups while UPower says their level is normal.
explanation: Devices such as Logitech HID++ mice and keyboards only report a coarse battery level (Normal, Low, …); UPower turns it into an approximate percentage that it marks "should be ignored". Powerdevil reads the battery through Solid, which has no battery level, so it compared that approximate percentage with the peripheral low-battery threshold and alerted whenever the device reappeared with e.g. 10%. Before alerting about a peripheral, powerdevil now reads the device's UPower BatteryLevel and, when the device uses a coarse level, only alerts if that level is Low or Critical.

commits.message:
daemon: Trust UPower's battery level for peripheral low battery alerts

Devices like Logitech mice only report a coarse level, and UPower marks
the percentage it derives as one to ignore, yet it still triggered alerts.
For such devices, notify only when the level itself is low or critical.

BUG: 457893

media.caption: Pure master: a Logitech M705 reporting Normal level with an approximate 10% ("should be ignored") is connected, and a "Mouse Battery Low (10% Remaining)" popup appears
With the fix, the same device connects with no popup

review.text: The diagnosis is right: Solid's Battery has no coarse battery level, so powerdevil compares UPower's approximate percentage with the threshold. The patch works around the missing Solid API with a synchronous system-bus D-Bus Get and hardcoded UpDeviceLevel numbers inside powerdevil, bypassing the Solid abstraction powerdevil uses for everything else. The proper fix is to expose the level in Solid (KF) and use it from powerdevil. That also lets powerdevil react to Normal→Low level changes, a case the notes say this patch misses.
changes: solid: add a battery level property (e.g. Solid::Battery::batteryLevel() with None/Low/Critical/Normal/High/Full and a change signal) to the UPower backend, read from UPower's BatteryLevel
powerdevil: use that Solid property instead of a raw D-Bus Get with magic numbers; for devices with a coarse level, alert on the level becoming Low/Critical rather than on the approximate percentage
